description: Ground truth for DVNA (Damn Vulnerable NodeJS Application) — a realistic Express/Sequelize application. Vulnerabilities are documented in the DVNA wiki and confirmed by manual code review. No VULN annotations exist in the source code — this is a clean real-world evaluation target.

scan_metadata.note: DVNA is a realistic Node.js application demonstrating all OWASP Top 10 categories. It uses the same Express + Sequelize stack as the synthetic js-ts-sqli benchmark but is not synthetic — it is a working web application.

expected_findings.description: req.body.login concatenated directly into raw Sequelize query string — classic authentication SQLi allowing login bypass via ' OR '1'='1
expected_findings.code_pattern: "SELECT name,id FROM Users WHERE login='" + req.body.login + "'"

expected_findings.description: req.body.address concatenated into exec() shell command — attacker can append ; rm -rf / or pipe to arbitrary commands
node-serialize.unserialize() on user-supplied file contents — CVE-class RCE via IIFE payload in serialized object
libxmljs.parseXmlString called with noent:true — allows XXE attacks reading local files (/etc/passwd) or SSRF via HTTP entities
Password reset token is MD5(username) — MD5 is cryptographically broken and the token is trivially predictable given any username

known_issues_outside_deepguard_scope.note: res.redirect(req.query.url) — unvalidated redirect. Deep-Guard has no open_redirect type; may appear as ssrf or auth_issue
mathjs.eval(req.body.eqn) — expression injection via math library. Deep-Guard may flag as command_injection

why_better_than_synthetic: DVNA source files contain zero VULN annotations — no comments labelling vulnerability locations or types. Any finding Deep-Guard produces must come from code analysis, not comment-reading. The code structure (real middleware stack, ORM callbacks, class-based services) mirrors production Node.js applications.
